habit_scope: habit Northwest and Southeast (HUD RSDG §4.1). Alternate in cold climates vs basement.
how_it_is_done: Site / termite prep as for CIP/CMU: strip organics; pull roots, stumps, scrap, and form stakes; soil termiticide where hazard; compact before footings (ORNL §2.4 / Ch 3; AF&PA Termites). Do not trade treatment for shields (D8).
Footings below local frost. Vented crawl: interior and exterior grade both count for frost because the space can freeze (ORNL Ch 3).

Walls: CIP, CMU, or piers. AF&PA Other Foundations: free-standing piers commonly 8–12 ft, or piers + curtain walls / grade beams — variants inside this method, not a separate type. HUD §4.1 names pier-and-beam + brick curtain as an economical crawl alternate. Height is what separates crawl vs basement (HUD §4.1).

Dampproof/waterproof generally not required if crawl floor is at or above exterior grade and drainage is adequate (ORNL Ch 3). If the crawl floor is below grade on tight soil, run a basement-like perimeter drain (maybe a sump) — same tile family as CIP/CMU, still not PWF.
Ground cover: 6-mil poly over all exposed soil, 12-in laps, edges to wall (ORNL §3.2 radon/ground cover). AF&PA: 12 in earth-to-girder, 18 in earth-to-joist; treat wood if missed.

Crawl vents vs unvented = D1 variants (c-P05-D1-crawl-vent): AF&PA 1/150 (or 1/1500 with 6-mil + operable louvers); ORNL energy model 1/1500 and prefers unvented/semi-heated but agencies often will not allow year-round closed vents; HUD has no vent-ratio. Follow the adopted IRC/energy code. Do not vent a plenum crawl. Venting is not reliable radon control (ORNL Ch 3).
Posts: D7 / c-P07-D7-post-clearance — AF&PA 1 in above concrete / 6 in above earth vs ORNL 8 in above interior grade. Use the stricter of adopted code vs 8 in when following ORNL.
Grade away 5% (6 in in 10 ft). Treated sill, inspectable. Floor framing (P07) sits on this wall/pier system. Glue T&G and seal penetrations over crawl for air/radon (ORNL §3.2).

Backfill only where walls are below grade; waterproof-before-backfill still applies to that below-grade face. Floor-in-before-significant-backfill (HUD §4.5) if the crawl wall is a stem that needs top brace.
trades: ORNL checklist: grading / construction / landscape contractors
AF&PA: job foreman, subcontractors, building inspector — no crew size
tools_equipment: Not a tool list in sources. Named: form stakes (pull before treatment); same footing-bucket widths as basement when a wall is used (HUD §4.4).
inspection_hold_points: Footing inspection before pour; no frozen subgrade (ORNL).
Soil treatment before covering the crawl floor / before any slab pour in the crawl.
Clearances 12 in girder / 18 in joist (AF&PA); post clearance D7.
Vent vs unvented per adopted IRC/energy code, not a winner from this set (D1).
If below-grade wall is waterproofed, that coating before backfill (ORNL).
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit in the Northwest and Southeast (HUD §4.1). In cold climates it beats basement when the water table is within ~8 ft (ORNL §1.3 veto on basement) or when the program does not want a full basement. Piers are the light-touch crawl variant (AF&PA; HUD).
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Not the Wasatch/Logan basement habit. Vented crawl in a hard-frost climate freezes the space — interior and exterior grade both count (ORNL Ch 3). Do not treat D1 vent ratios as settled. Mapped floodplain: a crawl with interior grade below exterior grade on all sides is classed as a basement (HUD §4.1).
why_tier1_never_learned_it: In NW/SE they did learn it — it is the regional habit. In cold-climate basement markets it is the cheaper/shallower alt when a basement is vetoed.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
risk_if_swapped_late: Crawl vs basement after permit changes excavation, drainage, vents, and first-floor height. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: Crawl is the usual foundation in the Northwest and Southeast: short wall or piers, wood kept off the dirt, plastic on the ground. Vents vs no vents is a code call — follow the adopted energy/IRC, do not pick a 1991 or 2001 number yourself. In cold country this is the backup when you do not want a full basement.
spanish_summary: El crawl es el hábito en el Noroeste y el Sureste: pared baja o pilas, madera lejos de la tierra, plástico en el piso. Si se ventila o no lo decide el código adoptado, no un número de 1991. En clima frío es la alternativa cuando no quieren sótano.

HUD RSDG is an IRC companion. Crawl vent vs unvented: follow adopted IRC/energy code, not AF&PA 1/150 or ORNL 1991 alone. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. No R403/R404 in sources (gap-sop-irc-section-numbers).
